en.name: Pecans, chopped
en.summary: Chopped pecans keep 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and 2 years in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). No room-temperature timeline is given for them, and that omission is the advice: once a pecan is cut up, the cupboard is not really where it belongs.
en.pantry: There is no published cupboard figure for chopped pecans. Chopping multiplies the cut surface, and every cut surface is fresh oil meeting air — pecans are among the most fragile nuts to begin with, and pieces go rancid noticeably faster than halves. If you must keep a bag out, keep it sealed, dark, cool and short-term, and taste a few before you bake with them. The better plan is simply to buy halves and chop them as you need them.
en.fridge: 12 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in an airtight jar. This is the default home for chopped pecans, and the reason cold works so well is that the failure here is chemical rather than microbial: nothing is growing, the fat is oxidising, and low temperature slows that down dramatically. Keep them sealed hard — pecans are fatty and mild, and they will take on the smell of onions, garlic or anything else strong in the fridge.
en.freezer: 2 years at −18 °C (0 °F), and this is where a big bag should live. Pecan pieces contain almost no water, so freezing does not change the texture at all, and you can scatter them straight from frozen into a batter or over a tart. Freeze them flat in a bag with the air pressed out, or in a rigid tub, and portion so you are not opening the whole lot each time.
en.thawing: No thawing needed — use them from frozen. If you take out the whole bag, let it come back to room temperature sealed so condensation does not settle on the pieces.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp or paint-like taste, which is rancid pecan oil.
A smell like old cooking oil or crayons instead of sweet and buttery.
Soft, chewy pieces rather than crisp ones — moisture has got in.
Mould or a musty smell in a bag that got damp.
tips: Buy halves and chop them yourself; pieces are already further along the clock.
Freeze the bulk and keep a small jar in the fridge for baking.
Taste before you bake — rancidity carries straight into the pie.
Store in opaque, airtight containers; light drives oxidation as surely as heat.

faq.q: How long do chopped pecans keep?
faq.a: 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 2 years in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Can you keep chopped pecans in a cupboard?
faq.a: No cupboard timeline is published for them. The cut surfaces expose a lot of fragile oil to air, so chopped pecans are stored cold.

faq.q: How can you tell if pecans have gone bad?
faq.a: Taste one. Rancid pecans are bitter and taste of old oil, and the flavour carries straight through anything you bake with them.

zh.name: 胡桃碎
zh.summary: 胡桃碎放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍可放 2 年。它沒有常溫的期限數據，而這個「沒有」本身就是建議：胡桃一旦切碎，櫥櫃就不是它該待的地方了。
zh.pantry: 胡桃碎沒有公布的櫥櫃期限。切碎會把切面成倍放大，而每一個切面都是新鮮的油直接碰到空氣——胡桃本來就是最脆弱的堅果之一，碎粒油耗的速度明顯比整半顆快。真的要放外面，就密封、避光、陰涼，而且盡快用完，烘焙前先嚐幾粒。更好的做法很簡單：買整半顆，要用多少切多少。
zh.fridge: 氣密罐放 4 °C 以下，12 個月。這是胡桃碎預設的歸宿；低溫之所以這麼有效，是因為它壞掉的方式是化學性的而不是微生物性的：沒有東西在生長，是油脂在氧化，而低溫會大幅拖慢這件事。請確實密封——胡桃油多味淡，冰箱裡的洋蔥、大蒜或任何味道重的東西，它都會照單全收。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 2 年，大包裝就該放這裡。胡桃碎幾乎不含水，冷凍完全不改變質地，可以直接從冷凍撒進麵糊或鋪在塔上。請壓出空氣、平放密封，或用硬盒裝，並且分裝，免得每次都得打開一整包。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍，直接從冷凍用。如果整包拿出來，請維持密封回到室溫，免得結露在碎粒上。
spoilage: 嚐起來苦、尖銳或有油漆味，那是胡桃油油耗。
聞起來像久放的食用油或蠟筆，而不是奶香甜香。
咬起來軟韌而不脆——水氣跑進去了。
受潮的袋子長霉或有霉味。
tips: 買整半顆自己切；已經切碎的等於走在前面。
大量冷凍，冷藏留一小罐烘焙用。
烘焙前先嚐一下，油耗味會整個進到派裡。
用不透光的氣密容器；光線和溫度一樣會推動氧化。

faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 2 年。
它沒有公布的櫥櫃期限。切面把大量脆弱的油脂暴露在空氣中，所以胡桃碎是低溫保存的。
吃一粒。油耗的胡桃會苦、有久放的油味，而且這個味道會原封不動穿過整個烘焙成品。
